newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations perk up in latest week -JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations perk up in latest week -JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European monetary union in 1999 stabilised over the past week, with the perceived probability of Italy taking part back above 50 percent, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed.

Financial prices indicate that the probability assumed by the market of Italy, Spain and Sweden joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU climbed during the week, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator."

The probability of Italy starting EMU in 1999 rose four points to 53 percent and Spain rose three points to 68 percent - both back to levels of one month ago. Sweden, meantime, rose four points to 60 percent this week but is still down six points from last month.

The calculator showed the probability of France starting EMU remains 100 percent but expectations of Belgium's participation remained shy of certainty, edging down two points to 97 percent in the latest week.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.
Elsewhere, expectations of first-wave EMU participation in Ireland, Portugal, Denmark and the UK all climbed while Finland slipped two points to 77 percent.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
